subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Identifying metal ions (flame tests and hydroxide precipitates)
Testing for anions (carbonates, halides and sulfates)

questions.q: What happens to the reactivity of the Group 1 alkali metals as you go down the group?
questions.explain: Reactivity increases down Group 1 because the outer electron is lost more easily.

questions.q: How would you test for hydrogen gas?
options: A lighted splint produces a squeaky pop
questions.explain: Hydrogen gives a characteristic squeaky pop with a lighted splint.

questions.q: Which observation confirms the presence of oxygen gas?
options: A lighted splint produces a squeaky pop
questions.explain: Oxygen relights a glowing splint because it supports combustion.

questions.q: Which gas turns limewater milky (cloudy)?
questions.explain: Carbon dioxide turns limewater milky by forming insoluble calcium carbonate.

questions.q: What flame colour does a lithium compound produce in a flame test?
questions.explain: Lithium ions give a crimson (red) flame colour.

questions.q: A green flame in a flame test indicates the presence of which metal ion?
questions.explain: Copper ions produce a green flame colour.

questions.q: How can you test whether a compound contains carbonate ions?
options: Add dilute acid and test the gas released with limewater
questions.explain: Carbonates fizz with dilute acid, releasing carbon dioxide that turns limewater milky.

questions.q: After acidifying with dilute nitric acid, which reagent is added to test for halide ions?
questions.explain: Silver nitrate forms coloured silver halide precipitates with halide ions.

questions.q: Why does reactivity increase as you go down Group 1?
options: The outer electron is further from the nucleus and lost more easily
The atoms gain electrons more easily
questions.explain: A larger atom holds its outer electron less strongly, so it is lost more readily.

questions.q: Why does the reactivity of the Group 7 halogens decrease down the group?
options: It becomes harder to gain an electron as the outer shell is further from the nucleus
It becomes easier to lose an electron
questions.explain: Larger halogen atoms attract an incoming electron less strongly, reducing reactivity.

questions.q: A halogen will displace another halogen from a solution of its salt if it is...
options: More reactive than the halogen in the salt
Less reactive than the halogen in the salt
questions.explain: A more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive one from its compounds.

questions.q: Sodium hydroxide is added to two solutions: one forms a green precipitate, the other a brown precipitate. Which ions are present?
options: Iron(II) gives green and iron(III) gives brown
Iron(III) gives green and iron(II) gives brown
Copper gives green and iron gives brown
questions.explain: Iron(II) hydroxide is green and iron(III) hydroxide is brown.

questions.q: Aluminium, calcium and magnesium ions all form a white precipitate with sodium hydroxide. How can aluminium be identified?
options: Its white precipitate redissolves when excess sodium hydroxide is added
questions.explain: Aluminium hydroxide dissolves in excess sodium hydroxide, unlike calcium or magnesium hydroxide.

questions.q: What are the precipitate colours when silver nitrate is added to chloride, bromide and iodide solutions?
options: Chloride white, bromide cream, iodide yellow
Chloride yellow, bromide cream, iodide white
Chloride cream, bromide white, iodide yellow
questions.explain: Silver chloride is white, silver bromide is cream and silver iodide is yellow.

questions.q: What happens when chlorine gas is held over damp litmus paper?
options: It bleaches the litmus paper white
questions.explain: Chlorine bleaches damp litmus paper, turning it white.

questions.q: Why are the Group 0 noble gases very unreactive?
options: They have a full, stable outer shell of electrons
They have a single outer electron
They have very large atomic radii
questions.explain: A full outer shell means noble gases have no tendency to gain, lose or share electrons.

questions.q: A solution is acidified with dilute nitric acid and silver nitrate is added, forming a cream precipitate. Which ion is present?
questions.explain: A cream silver halide precipitate indicates bromide ions.

questions.q: Adding dilute hydrochloric acid then barium chloride to a solution produces a white precipitate. Which ion does this confirm?
questions.explain: A white precipitate of barium sulfate confirms the presence of sulfate ions.

questions.q: Chlorine water is added to a colourless solution of potassium bromide. What is observed and why?
options: The solution turns orange as chlorine displaces bromine
No reaction, because bromine is more reactive than chlorine
The solution turns colourless as bromine displaces chlorine
questions.explain: Chlorine is more reactive, so it displaces bromine, which colours the solution orange.

questions.q: A strip of magnesium is placed in blue copper(II) sulfate solution. What is observed?
options: The blue colour fades and a copper coating forms on the magnesium
A gas is released with a squeaky pop
questions.explain: Magnesium is more reactive, so it displaces copper, which deposits as the blue solution fades.

specSource: OCR GCSE (9–1) Chemistry (Gateway A) (J248) specification; Predicting & Identifying Reactions
